title: Applying LFQRatio Normalization in Quantitative Proteomic Analysis of Microbial Co-culture Systems
author: Mengxun Shi

steps.title: Prepare 1 M Tris‑HCl (pH 8.5) solution
steps.instruction: Weigh 12.114 g Tris, dissolve in 80 mL HPLC‑grade water, adjust pH to 8.5 with HCl, and bring the final volume to 100 mL with HPLC‑grade water. Store at room temperature.

steps.title: Prepare 1 M DTT solution
steps.instruction: Dissolve 1.542 g DTT in 10 mL HPLC‑grade water, aliquot, and store at –20 °C or use immediately; discard after one freeze‑thaw cycle.

steps.title: Prepare Lysis buffer (20 mL)
steps.instruction: Combine 400 mg SDS (2 % w/v), 0.8 mL 1 M Tris‑HCl (pH 8.5) for a final 40 mM concentration, 1.2 mL 1 M DTT for a final 60 mM concentration, add HPLC‑grade water to a total volume of 20 mL, and mix thoroughly.

substeps.instruction: Weigh 400 mg SDS and add to a beaker.
Add HPLC‑grade water up to 20 mL total volume.

steps.title: Prepare Urea buffer (500 µL)
steps.instruction: Dissolve 240 mg urea (8 M final) in a LoBind tube, add 50 µL 1 M Tris‑HCl (pH 8.5) for 100 mM final, add 2.5 µL 1 M DTT for 5 mM final, and bring the volume to 500 µL with HPLC‑grade water. Prepare fresh; use within a few hours.

substeps.instruction: Weigh 240 mg urea into a 1.5 mL LoBind tube.
Add HPLC‑grade water up to 500 µL total.

steps.title: Prepare 100 mM iodoacetamide (IAA) solution
steps.instruction: Dissolve 0.0185 g IAA in 1 mL HPLC‑grade water, wrap the tube in foil to protect from light, and use fresh.

steps.title: Prepare 1 mg/mL trypsin stock
steps.instruction: Add 20 µL trypsin resuspension buffer to one vial containing 20 µg lyophilized sequencing‑grade modified trypsin, vortex briefly, and store at –80 °C for up to 1 month.

steps.title: Prepare 100 mM CaCl₂ solution
steps.instruction: Dissolve 1.47 g CaCl₂ in 100 mL HPLC‑grade water; store at room temperature.

steps.title: Prepare 50 mM Tris‑HCl (pH 8.5)/10 mM CaCl₂ buffer
steps.instruction: Mix 1 mL 1 M Tris‑HCl (pH 8.5) for 50 mM final, 2 mL 100 mM CaCl₂ for 10 mM final, and 17 mL HPLC‑grade water; total volume 20 mL.

steps.title: Prepare MS loading buffer
steps.instruction: In a fume hood, combine 30 µL ACN (3 % v/v), 1 µL TFA (0.1 % v/v), and 969 µL HPLC‑grade water; mix gently.

steps.title: Prepare 80 % ACN solution
steps.instruction: In a fume hood, mix 800 mL ACN with 200 mL HPLC‑grade water to obtain 80 % (v/v) ACN; store at room temperature.

steps.title: Prepare MS mobile phase solvents
steps.instruction: Solvent A: mix 1 mL formic acid (0.1 % v/v) with 999 mL HPLC‑grade water. Solvent B: mix 1 mL formic acid (0.1 % v/v) with 999 mL 80 % ACN. Prepare both in a fume hood.

substeps.instruction: Solvent A: 1 mL formic acid (0.1 % v/v) + 999 mL water.
Solvent B: 1 mL formic acid (0.1 % v/v) + 999 mL 80 % ACN.

steps.title: Grow bacterial cultures and harvest cells
steps.instruction: Cultivate the monocultures or co‑culture to the desired growth phase, measure optical density (OD) at the appropriate wavelength, and centrifuge 20 mL of culture at 4,000 × g for 10 min at 4 °C in 50 mL centrifuge tubes. Pellets may be stored at –20 °C for up to 1 month before processing.

steps.title: Wash cell pellets
steps.instruction: Resuspend each pellet in 10 mL PBS, centrifuge again under the same conditions, discard supernatant, and keep pellets on ice or store at –20 °C for up to 1 month.

steps.title: Resuspend pellets in lysis buffer with protease inhibitor
steps.instruction: Add 500 µL lysis buffer per 1 OD unit (e.g., OD = 2 → 1 mL lysis buffer) to the pellet, then add 100× Halt protease inhibitor cocktail at 1 µL per 100 µL total volume (e.g., ~7 µL for a ~700 µL mixture). Mix gently.

steps.title: Freeze‑thaw cells
steps.instruction: Freeze the resuspended cells at –80 °C for >16 h, then thaw quickly in a 37 °C water bath for 3–5 min, and immediately place on ice. Frozen pellets can remain in lysis buffer at –80 °C for ~1 month.

steps.title: Transfer lysate to pre‑cooled LoBind tubes
steps.instruction: Label and pre‑cool 1.5 mL LoBind microcentrifuge tubes on ice, then transfer the lysed cell suspension into them; keep all samples on ice for the remainder of the procedure.

steps.title: Add glass beads
steps.instruction: Add ~500 µL of 425–600 µm acid‑washed glass beads to each tube, ensuring 2–3 mm of liquid remains above the settled beads.

steps.title: Disrupt cells by vortexing
steps.instruction: Vortex each tube 20 times using a multi‑tube vortex attachment: 30 s vortex followed by 30 s on ice, repeat for a total of 20 cycles.

steps.title: Heat lysates
steps.instruction: Incubate the tubes at 95 °C in a dry heat block for 5 min.

steps.title: Clarify lysate by centrifugation
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at 15,000 × g for 10 min at 4 °C, collect the supernatant into a fresh 1.5 mL LoBind tube, and store at –20 °C for up to ~1 month. Optional: determine protein concentration (e.g., detergent‑compatible Bradford assay) and assess by SDS‑PAGE.

steps.title: Clean‑up proteins with 2D Clean‑Up kit
steps.instruction: Follow the manufacturer’s instructions for the 2D Clean‑Up kit, using the prepared urea buffer as the resuspension buffer. After the wash step, protein pellets may be stored in wash buffer at –20 °C for up to 1 week. Once dried, proceed directly to downstream digestion.

substeps.instruction: Add precipitant to the crude protein sample as instructed.
Wash the pellet with wash buffer; store at –20 °C if needed (up to 1 week).
Resuspend the dried pellet in urea buffer.

description: Validation of protocol This protocol or parts of it has been used and validated in the following research article(s): • Shi et al. [11] LFQRatio: A normalization method to decipher quantitative proteome changes in microbial coculture systems. Journal of Proteome Research (Figure 9). • Kratzl et al. [21] Pseudomonas putida as saviour for troubled Synechococcus elongatus in a synthetic co-culture–interaction studies based on a multi-OMICs approach. Communications Biology (Figure 4).
